#41 + #36 — architect responsibility levels. An architect is responsible for a scope: one application, one team, one department, or the whole organization. The level clamps the 🏢 scope switcher — and every application, wave, and aggregate you can see follows.
#41 — multi-tenancy. Organizations are isolated: switching one changes every application, wave, and aggregate you can see. Within your organization, scope further to a department or a team — teams staff architects, project managers, and migrators, and every application belongs to exactly one team.

      ⓘ How this navigation is governed — RBAC, tenancy & credentials #36/#41
      #36 item 2 — RBAC-driven navigation (implemented). Switch persona above: nav entries, deep links, and in-page verbs all derive from resource:verb scopes — Migrator sees no Administration entries and cannot re-validate waves; Project mgr is read-only; gated buttons carry the missing scope on hover; disallowed deep links redirect Home with a warning. Try #scr=config as Architect. Tenancy locks (#41): the Project manager and Migrator are locked to their team's scope; the Architect chooses a responsibility level (application › team › department › organization — the selector beside the 🏢 switcher) that clamps the scope; the Program manager sees the whole organization plus the cross-team coordination view in Migration waves. Admin vs Platform admin: the Admin is an organization admin (org-locked like every other persona); the Platform admin operates above tenancy — provisioning organizations, with every cross-org access audit-logged (#42) in Administration → Controls → Organizations.
      #41 — multi-tenancy (implemented, user request). The 🏢 switcher in the masthead scopes everything to an organization → department → team: organizations are isolated (try Meridian Health — 3 apps, no waves), teams staff architects/project managers/migrators, and every application belongs to exactly one team. Admin: Administration → Controls → Teams. Try #scr=inventory&org=mrd. Credentials are team-owned too (#15, user request): the Credentials view shows exactly the current scope's credentials (every credential belongs to one team, like applications) — as Migrator you see and manage Claims' 3; as Admin, all 4 Northwind credentials; switch org as Platform admin to see Meridian's. As Program mgr, the waves screen gains the cross-team coordination card (Wave 4 spans 3 teams); the Project mgr is locked to team Claims.

                        Import applications

                        Per-step validation kills the silent failure modes at the step that causes them #44

                        Import applications — step 3 of 5 #44

                        1. Source
                        2. Credentials
                        3. Repository
                        4. Business service
                        5. Review

                        Source: choose SCM / binary / custom — the wizard remembers team-typical defaults #2

                        Credentials: the owning team's credentials (#41/#15 — what the imported application can use), filtered to the selected scheme's kinds, with the test action inline R2-15

                        Scheme, host reachability, and branch are validated now — not at analysis time #39

                        ⚠

                        Scheme requires a different credential kind

                        ssh:// requires an SSH-key credential; the selected credential is username/password. Also: agent runs clone over HTTPS only (agentic-controller#240) — suggest https:// URL with a PAT.

                        Branch list resolved from the remote — free-text typos can't silently analyze the wrong tree.

                        Filtered to the kinds this repository scheme supports; test action attached R2-15

                        Business service: pre-selected from the application record; archetypes ride along #33

                        Review: import plan as a diff — what will be created, what will be reused, what will fail validation now instead of at run time #44

                        Step validates via the same API the run will use — no mock checks.
                        Implements: #44 · #39 · #1177 (branch resolution) · issue 15 (credential test) · comment 10's "discovery should carry validation" principle.

                        The rate field is the monetary amount assigned to token usage per gateway — editing it re-prices that gateway’s showback (tokens × rate). Amounts display in the currency chosen with the Currency selector — Auto derives it from the selected language’s primary country (USD default) — the rate is stored in USD and converted at render (demo FX rates).                                     Change CA trust

                                    Applying runs a connection test before the change lands — a failing test keeps the previous trust material. In-flight runs are unaffected: they finish on the gateway configuration they started with. Every change is recorded in the audit log. upstream

                                    Revoke API key?

                                    The key stops authenticating immediately. Anything still using it (automation, integrations) will fail with 401 until re-issued. c9

                                    Delete tracker jira-cloud-prod?

                                    This tracker is referenced by 2 migration waves — Wave 3 (invoicing, payments-api, ledger-sync) and Wave 4 (claims-web, risk-scoring) — with 14 open tickets. Deleting it stops all ticket sync for those waves immediately.

                                    The affected waves are named because the API answers which resources use this tracker — today the belongs-to-only relations make that unrenderable, so deletions break exports silently. #33

                                    Enable insecure communication?

                                    This disables TLS certificate verification for tracker jira-dc-legacy: credentials and ticket payloads become readable to anyone who can intercept the connection (MITM).

                                    The change is recorded in the audit log: who, when, from where. #42
